title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving health assistance to the most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas of Bu’aale

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project targets undeserved populations in Bu’aale District affected by recurring climate shocks, displacement, limited access to health services, and disease outbreaks. A recent health assessment undertaken in April 2025 highlighted the plight faced by the communities to include lack of access to essential health services. The recurrent drought and floods in the area has limited access to health care characterized by poor health indicators among the population most of whom are IDPs. This poor state coupled by weak response by actors calls for an integrated approach targeted at improving access to health services to reducing mortalities and controlling and/or prevent disease outbreaks thus minimizing further displacements. ltbrgtTo address these urgent needs, BADEF proposes a health intervention aimed at delivering integrated, life-saving primary healthcare services to the most vulnerable populations, with a particular focus on women, children, persons with disabilities, and internally displaced persons (IDPs). The intervention is designed to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality through the provision of an essential package of integrated primary healthcare services. These include outpatient consultations, maternal and reproductive health, routine immunization, nutrition screening, management of waterborne and communicable diseases, trauma and emergency care, and specialized services such as gender-based violence (GBV) response and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS). Patient pathways within supported facilities will be reorganized to systematically identify and respond to the needs of vulnerable populations, including women, children under five, elderly persons, and persons with disabilities.ltbrgtThe project will support one fixed health facility ( Badef Buale Health center an MCH) and one mobile outreach services to ensure access across hard-to-reach and underserved areas. Core activities will include immunization for children under five and pregnant women, outpatient treatment for common illnesses such as malaria and respiratory infections, reproductive health services including antenatal, delivery, and postnatal care, and screening for malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies. To enhance service coverage, the project will conduct at least 15 mobile outreach sessions per month, targeting rural villages and IDP settlements of Angole Uen, Anole, Arabow, Bandar Jidiid, and Bu Buule.ltbrgtA total of 28,629 individuals are expected to benefit directly from the health services provided. To ensure inclusive and dignified care, the project will equip one health facility with essential medical supplies and disability-friendly infrastructure such as ramps. All frontline health workers will be trained on immunization management of childhood diseases (IMCI), disability inclusion, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), and referral mechanisms for gender-based violence (GBV) and child protection cases.ltbrgtCommunity engagement will be central to the project. BADEF will work closely with the Ministry of Health, local leaders, and community-based structures to mobilize participation and build ownership. Community feedback mechanisms will be established at all service delivery points to promote accountability and ensure that services remain responsive to community needs.ltbrgtThis project aims not only to reduce preventable illness and death but also to strengthen the resilience of the local health system. By promoting inclusive, community-driven healthcare and building local capacity, BADEF seeks to ensure that gains made through this project are sustained beyond the project period.ltbrgtlt/pgt
